rationale: A quiet beginning: the camera opens tight on the small boy from behind and reveals outward to the whole kampung while he walks up the plank walkway toward the outhouse, carrying the village's lack of plumbing into view.

filmIssues: The pull-back is clearly visible across the contact sheet: the opening frame is tight on the boy and plank walkway, while successive frames reveal the outhouse, surrounding kampung houses, palms and stream.
The movement expresses the scene's story: starting with the small boy carrying a bucket and widening to show the impoverished village and the outhouse that embody the lack of plumbing.
The boy, bucket and hand remain together with no obvious tearing, doubled edges, halo or ghost left on the walkway as he advances.
No cut-out layer clips the frame awkwardly; the boy remains fully inside the frame throughout.
The first frame works as a focused opening picture and the final frame is a balanced, complete view of the kampung that works well as the held reading image.
The dust effect is subtle and does not obscure the subject or undermine the flat-ink 1950s print appearance.
